title: The Fyre Festival Fiasco
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Fyre Festival, the 2017 Bahamas music festival that was promoted heavily but collapsed on arrival. They trace organizer Billy McFarland's earlier ventures (Spling social ad platform, the Magnus metal debit-card "credit card" and its Soho House-style club perks, and the Fyre talent-booking app), how the festival was hyped through influencer posts and a promo shoot, the scramble to find a site on Great Exuma after the Pablo Escobar island claim, cash-flow problems and the RFID wristband scheme, the chaotic April 28 arrival, the stranding at the airport, fraud convictions, prison time, the investor restitution question, NYC VIP Access, McFarland's later Phoenix festival, and the brand's sale to LimeWire. The episode closes with a listener mail about the McGuffin concept.

entities.name: Hype: Inside the Fyre Festival in the Golden Age of Grift

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Fyre Festival topic and mention the two documentaries about it.

segments.title: Billy McFarland's early startups
segments.summary: Background on organizer Billy McFarland, his childhood company, Spling social ad platform funded partly by Bucknell seed money, and dropping out of college.

segments.title: Magnus metal card
segments.summary: The Magnus card was a metal card that copied debit card data and offered club and loft perks that were not delivered, funded by spending beyond its income.

segments.title: Fyre app and the plan for a festival
segments.summary: McFarland created the Fyre talent-booking app to prop up Magnus, then conceived a music festival to promote the app, with a spring 2017 target set in fall 2016.

segments.title: Hype and promo video
segments.summary: Festival was built on hype: PR firms hired, a promo shoot in the Bahamas with models, and the promise of luxury and a private island; the promo video was the only real asset.

segments.title: Orange tile campaign and Kendall Jenner post
segments.summary: Influencers posted orange squares driving ticket sales, a paid Kendall Jenner post hinted at Kanye West, and tickets sold quickly.

segments.title: Site search and island time
segments.summary: After the Pablo Escobar island claim drew objection, the site moved to Roker Point on Great Exuma; forty-five days were allotted to build the village, and island time slowed work.

segments.title: Fire Tour, cash crunch, and RFID wristbands
segments.summary: Canceled pop-up Fire Tour concerts left cash short; organizers used preloaded RFID wristbands to fund spending on site.

segments.title: Eve of festival and Blink-182 withdrawal
segments.summary: Ticket holders found no updates; critics were deleted; the night before, VIPs were told to skip the first weekend, Blink-182 pulled out, and heavy rain halted setup.

segments.title: Festival day chaos and stranding
segments.summary: Arrivals on April 28 were bussed to a bar and handed FEMA tents; belongings were dumped, alcohol was handed out, attendees were stranded by a regatta weekend and locked in the airport, and the infamous styrofoam cheese sandwich was shown.

segments.title: Postponement and ticket holders
segments.summary: The festival was officially postponed; media investigations revealed financial crimes; ticket holders and vendors were left unpaid while investors were prioritized for repayment.

segments.title: Fraud charges, SEC case, and lawsuits
segments.summary: McFarland was charged over about $24 million from investors, sentenced to six years, and faced lawsuits; he allegedly lied about finances, and the hosts question where the money went.

segments.title: NYC VIP Access scam
segments.summary: While out on bail McFarland started NYC VIP Access, fronted by Frank Tribble, using the Fyre mailing list to sell fake event tickets.

segments.title: Prison and COVID
segments.summary: McFarland's prison experience: a COVID-related release request was denied, he contracted COVID, and he launched a podcast from prison; he was released early.

segments.title: Phoenix festival and Fyre brand sale
segments.summary: McFarland held a Phoenix festival in Honduras that was poorly attended; French Montana performed; the Fyre brand was sold on eBay to LimeWire.

segments.title: Documentary controversies
segments.summary: Hosts note that one documentary paid McFarland for an interview and the other was partnered with a PR firm that scrubbed negative comments; the Netflix film did not include McFarland.

segments.title: McGuffin listener mail
segments.summary: A listener explains the McGuffin as an item that could be swapped without changing the plot; the hosts debate examples like the Maltese Falcon.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing remarks and show credits, with an invitation to send email to the show.
